question:
A 27-year-old G2 woman at approximately 35-36 weeks gestation presents to labor and delivery with
contractions occurring every 3-5 minutes for the last hour. She has no access to her prenatal records,
cannot recall previous screening results, and reports no allergies. Her temperature is normal with
stable vital signs. Cervical examination shows 5 cm dilation with 60% effacement, and fetal monitoring
shows reassuring patterns. What is the most appropriate approach regarding group B streptococci
(GBS) screening and management in this case? Answer Choices: (A) Prophylactic antibiotics are only
indicated for patients with a history of neonatal GBS disease in a prior pregnancy. (B) Administer
antibiotics only if the patient develops a fever during labor. (C) Administer antibiotics only if the patient
reports a history of GBS colonization in a prior pregnancy. (D) Initiate prophylactic antibiotics. (E)
Obtain culture results and give antibiotic prophylaxis for GBS after her membranes rupture. (F) No
antibiotics are needed if the patient reports no known allergies or prior complications. (G) Initiate
antibiotics only if the patient progresses to active labor. (H) No antibiotics (I) Defer antibiotics until the
patient’s GBS status can be confirmed. (J) Administer antibiotics only if the patient’s membranes
rupture before delivery.

A. Initiate prophylactic antibiotics.
B. Initiate antibiotics only if the patient progresses to active labor.
C. No antibiotics are needed if the patient reports no known allergies or prior complications.
D. Prophylactic antibiotics are only indicated for patients with a history of neonatal GBS disease in a
prior pregnancy.
E. Defer antibiotics until the patient’s GBS status can be confirmed.
F. Administer antibiotics only if the patient reports a history of GBS colonization in a prior pregnancy.
G. No antibiotics
H. Administer antibiotics only if the patient’s membranes rupture before delivery.
I. Administer antibiotics only if the patient develops a fever during labor.
J. Obtain culture results and give antibiotic prophylaxis for GBS after her membranes rupture.
